messages.subject: warnings about prior prob of par g
parts:
Hi there.

I used mirt.model() to define prior probabilities(beta, 2, 5) of par g. 
Code:
modela<-mirt,model('
******
******
PRIOR=(1-50,g,beta,2,5) ')

When i ran this code:
moda<-mirt(data,model=modela,itemtype='3PL',method="QMCEM")
I received warnings: 

1: In ESTIMATION(data = data, model = model, group = rep("all",  ... :
  Lower and upper bound parameters (g and u) should use 'norm' (i.e., logit) prior
2: In ESTIMATION(data = data, model = model, group = rep("all",  ... :
  Lower and upper bound parameters (g and u) should use 'norm' (i.e., logit) prior
3: In ESTIMATION(data = data, model = model, group = rep("all",  ... :
  Lower and upper bound parameters (g and u) should use 'norm' (i.e., logit) prior
...

Did it mean that we can not defined beta(2,5) as prior distribution of par g?  There maybe other ways. Please help.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: warnings about prior prob of par g
parts:
Please read the mirt.model documentation about this. There are special priors that you should use for the g/u parameters because these are transformed internally during optimisation for better numerical stability. Also, this question has come up on the forum before, so feel free to search here for the answer as well. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: warnings about prior prob of par g

On Fri, Jan 5, 2018 at 12:13 PM, Can Yang <2525...@qq.com> wrote:
Oh, I have already read the manual and previous posts but I didn't understand well.If I wrote PRIOR=(1-50,g,expbeta,2,5) instead, I would received error report:
Error in UpdatePrior(PrepList, model, groupNames = Data$groupNames) : 
  Prior type specified in PRIOR = ... not available
This looks unusual. Could you provide a brief reproducible example with this prior? It's possible something broke in the latest update.
I tried other prior distributions for par g and found that (1-50,norm,0,1) would be accepted but g did not follow gaussian distribution obviously(it seemed like lnorm(0,1) or other types).

Actually, the norm prior is very appropriate here because the g parameter is transformed into a logit internally. Li Cai talks about this in Appendix A of the following article:

Cai, L.; Yang, H. S. & Hansen, M. Generalized Full-Information Item Bifactor Analysis
Psychological Methods, 2011, 16, 221-248

These pars might been transformed as you said. But I still don't know how to define par g in beta(2,5), neither (items,beta,alpha,beta) nor (items,expbeta,alpha,beta) can work.

Thank you very much.
